brief: #149 built the memory quota and #153 wired it into run-loop.sh step 4, so every iteration's row now carries quota {rc, over[]} and eight rows already have it. stall.mjs greps zero times for `quota`. A worker can therefore breach the read budget on every single iteration and never raise a signal in the report the manager plans from — the loop's own memory can grow unwatched, which is the failure mode the previous run died of. Make stall.mjs read it: a breach streak is a signal, and name the surface. Second half of c241, in the same brief: the runner's own three files (RUNLOG.jsonl, MANAGER-LOG.md, LEDGER-archive.md) are now the only unbounded growth left in this skill — report their size and their growth per iteration in the same table, so the next manager can see the line bend before it matters.
successLooksLike: `stall.mjs --report` names a quota-breach streak as a signal, proven on a staged set of rows that HEAD's own stall.mjs is silent about, and prints the loop's on-disk growth beside the verdict trend. Reports; never reverts.
avoid: Do not touch courtyard.html — this is a Harness brief and runlog flags a harness iteration that moves the source. Do not make a breach change a verdict: #153 decided deliberately that a 260 B cue is priced by the manager, not by a runner throwing away gate-passed work. A gate's PASS is only evidence about the fields it REPORTS, so show the new signal FIRING before you claim it works.
